title: What would happen if you stood on Venus? 🔥
subject: venus
description:
Would you rather try Venus or Mars? 👇

What would happen to you on the surface of Venus? The air pressure is about 92 times Earth's, the ground is about 860°F, and the Soviet lander Venera 13 lasted just 127 minutes there in 1982. NASA's Parker Solar Probe even caught the rock glowing through the clouds.

Sources: The Planetary Society ("What would it be like to stand on the surface of Venus?"), NASA / AGU ("First visible light images of Venus' surface from space captured by Parker Solar Probe", 2022), Guinness World Records ("Longest time survived on Venus by a spacecraft")
tags: what if you stood on venus

scenes.text: On Venus, you'd be crushed and cooked at once.
The air presses on you like 3,000 feet of ocean.
The ground is about 860 degrees Fahrenheit, hot enough to melt lead.
NASA's Parker Solar Probe caught that rock glowing through the clouds, "like a piece of iron pulled from a forge."
On March 1, 1982, the Soviet lander Venera 13 touched down, expected to last about 30 minutes.
It sent data for 127 minutes, then went silent. Nothing has lasted longer there since.
